name: Sanctuary
summary: Night Mother, peace bearer, hear this oath. I will harm none I see, so let those who would repay me with hatred be repaid in kind, let their weapons fall to the cool earth, let only repentance save them from you.
effects:
At sunset, you can invoke the Sanctuary Oath. While the Oath remains in place, you gain the following benefits:
When a Creature would attempt any kind of aggression against you, you can Coin-Flip to avoid it completely, no Action required.
You can make peace with any Beast by spending Sparks equal to its Tier. These obey you in loose terms and will not harm you or an Ally. Any aggression or an order intended to harm it breaks this effect.
The first effect you spend Sparks on each Round has a reduced cost by 1.
The Oath is broken on your part if you take any action intended to harm a Creature, unless they are Unholy.

name: The Door in the Night
summary: Luna, protector of travelers, open a way into your shaded hall. Give us safe passage and respite.
effects:
By spending 1 Minute, you can open a Door anywhere not in direct light. Doors all lead to the Evernight, which takes the form of a secluded wood at night. No living thing but plants can be seen there, Silverwoods above and Nightblooms below, and nothing edible grows within. However, its streams are full of clean, natural water.
From the Evernight, you can exit through any existing Door you conjure, allowing nearly instantaneous travel. You can have Doors up to your Faith there, and can banish any you wish at any time. Doors can be seen through from the Evernight, and affix to Spaces (moving when the Space does.) The Doors a Priest of Luna conjures are unique, and can only be accessed by them or Allies they lead through them.
When strong light like day or a lamp falls on a Door, it becomes invisible and intangible. You can also render any Door you create invisible and intangible as a 1 AP Interaction from the Evernight.
For 6 Sparks, you can recall a Door that you have previously banished.

summary: King of the Forge whose Light dwells in my hand, bathe these materials with your power and attend them to me. I call the Elements within and bid them obey, to change and become something new.
effects:
You can exchange the materials of Objects you Touch, changing one to another. The mechanics of the change follow the Primal Ring, which are the structure of Elements which Manus' Priests espouse to be the root of all things. The ring is made from the following five Elements:
These stand in a loop, with Water adjacent to Crystal. At the center of the Ring lies the sixth Element:
When you change something, first identify the strongest consistuent Element; Stone for rocks, Wood for a plank, Metal for a blade, etc. The result is an identically shaped re-imagining of the Target made from a pure form of an adjacent Element in the Ring. Life is an immutable Element, situated appart from the rest. For this reason, you cannot transmute a Creature, living, Undead, Demon, Celestial, etc.
When changing a thing, you can also decide the Phase of the Element, provided that Extreme Heat or Cold generated would not exceed your Virtue.
Plants present a unique exception to the immutability of Life, given that their principle Elements are Wood and Water in equal measure, with Life as a tertiary compound. This means that you can miraculously exchange the substance of a plant while leaving its Life unchanged, producing a Magical plant made from a different Element. Flowers of gold, trees made from granite, and grass formed from ice are all possible applications of this Prayer.
Finally, their are obstructions to Soulcasting. Materials that are Unholy, Magical, and otherwise unnatural, Arcane, Demonic, or otherwise estranged from the natural world cannot be effected. Likewise, while drinkable water can be made, edible food is impossible, because food's nutritive power stems from a complex blend of all Elements, and the results of Soulcasting are pure.
